root_cause: builtins.rs:64 cb() plus the any/all/find/position/take_while/drop_while arms (builtins.rs:436-455) and sort_by (456): the callback is analyzed once under pc = the collection's shape label (c.lab). The runtime helpers stop early on a callback result (anubis_any/all/find/position/take_while/drop_while, run.rs 2846-2855, 3058-3094), and sort_by calls the key function once per comparison, a data-dependent number of times (run.rs 2859-2875). So whether call n+1 happens depends on earlier callback results, but nothing raises the pc for it.

eval.rs:796-799 apply(): composed pairs run through self.apply(&h, args, p) and self.apply(&g, [inner], p) with the caller's path p. The secret label of the composed value itself (f.lab, set when the if chose it) never reaches the pc of those calls, unlike user, builtin and closure callees, which use pc ⊔ f.lab. value.rs raise_in_place does not reach the composed parts either, so their own labels stay PUB.

value.rs:798 join_fns maps (Summary, Env(e)) to Summary without adding e to the interpreter's per-lambda summaries, and value.rs:740 fns_leq treats any Env as ≤ Summary without checking e ⊑ summaries[id]. Only widening past CLOSURE_DEPTH records an env (eval.rs widen_to). In this program f is nested 3 deep in d's captures, so it is summarized with s=PUB. d(0)(0)(0) extracts that Summary(L) to the top level. Joining it with the fresh Env{s: SEC} of the same lambda (h) drops the secret env. analyze_lambda(Summary) then reads summaries[L] = {s: PUB}.

builtins.rs:525-560 reduce(): for reduce(list, a, b) the runtime folds with b only when a is not a closure (anubis_reduce, run.rs 2815-2828). The (y, x) order applies y via cb(it, &f, .., c.lab, p), so the pc is c.lab ⊔ y.lab only. The label that decides a's kind (a.lab, secret here) is joined only into the result ('decided'), not into the pc under which y's effects run.

eval.rs:1664-1666 method_call() evaluates every argument once, at the caller's pc, before dispatch. The runtime inlines the lowered arguments into each type arm of the match on the receiver's type name and passes only arity-1 of them (run.rs 4956-5001). An argument is therefore evaluated only inside the chosen arm, only if that method takes it, and under the dispatch condition. IFC v2 never raises the argument's evaluation by recv.lab and assumes it always runs.

builtins.rs:493 apply(): a list whose positions are unknown (items: None) is spread as exactly six copies of its element (vec![li.all.raise(xs.lab); 6]). The runtime passes the whole list (anubis_apply: f.call_closure(items), run.rs 2876-2881), so the 7th and later parameters get real elements. IFC v2 pads them with V::scalar(PUB) in analyze_lambda, and the same happens after resize for user-fn values.

value.rs:179 part_of_top() builds a top value with no functions. When widening folds a container (value.rs:620, at DATA_DEPTH, at SUMMARY_DEPTH=4 for summary-context arguments, or at a halved limit once a value exceeds MAX_NODES=256), its closures are kept only in the folded node's own fns. Any element, field or key read out of it (index_read, field_read, elems/iter_elem, bind_pattern, try_value, pop and others) loses them. Applying such a value does nothing: apply() iterates only fns.user, builtins, clos, composed and any, and top without fns means bottom.

builtins.rs:467-479 map_values applies the callback only when the argument has a map component (if let Some(x) = &m.map). A top argument, which may be any map, never has its callback analyzed. The runtime applies f to every value of the map (anubis_map_values, run.rs 3207-3214). Every other callback builtin handles top through elems().

eval.rs:514-548 call(), summary contexts. The joined arguments (contexts[callee].1) are shared by every pc, but the summary memo is keyed per pc: skey = (callee, [], pc). When a call at one pc grows the joined arguments, only that pc's memo is removed (line 538). A later call at another pc whose arguments are ⊑ the new join sees grew == false and returns that pc's memo (line 546), which was computed from the old, smaller arguments.

eval.rs:2170-2176 field_read() reads a map's key f as known[f] or other and raises only by the map's own lab. It ignores m.klab, the label of the computed keys, which decides whether key f is present at all. index_read (m[k]) does raise by klab. The method-call fallback (a map holding a closure under the method name, eval.rs method_call) and plain m.f reads both go through field_read.

builtins.rs:426-465: map, flat_map, filter, each, find, any, all, count, position, sort_by, partition, and reduce (through cb) pass shape = c.lab as the callback's pc and use c.lab as the result length label. Iterating a map yields its keys (anubis_iter), and how many keys there are depends on m.klab: computed keys can collide, and the last duplicate wins in a literal. for-loops use len_label (which includes klab), and map_values uses m.lab ⊔ klab, but the list HOFs do not.

value.rs fns_widened / eval.rs widen_to: closures nested past CLOSURE_DEPTH=3 are summarized per lambda, and summaries[L] joins the envs of every instance of L. The never-called secret chain s pollutes the summary that the public chain p reads when it is called: 'ANUBIS_SECRET_EXFILTRATION: [ifc2] in `main`: secret data reaches `println`'.

eval.rs:1664-1666 method_call() evaluates every argument before dispatch. Here the receiver is exactly Plain, whose get takes no argument after self, so the runtime never evaluates audit(k) (run.rs 4966-4980 passes arity-1 arguments per arm). IFC v2 analyzes audit(k) anyway and reports 'ANUBIS_IMPLICIT_FLOW: [ifc2] in `audit`: `println` runs under a condition a secret decides'.

eval.rs:490-550 call(): after CONTEXTS_PER_CALLEE=12 distinct argument contexts, every later call of a callee (at the same pc) shares one summary context whose arguments are the join of all of them. One secret call site (hidden, whose result is only declassified) therefore makes every later call of the helper secret, and the public println is refused ('ANUBIS_SECRET_EXFILTRATION: [ifc2] in `main`: secret data reaches `println`').

builtins.rs:456-460 sort_by returns list_of(elems(&c), c.lab ⊔ r.deep()). A list's lab stands for both its length and its order, so a secret sort key also marks the length secret, although sort_by preserves length (run.rs 2859-2875). len(ranked) becomes secret, and the loop's println is refused ('ANUBIS_IMPLICIT_FLOW: [ifc2] in `main`: `println` runs under a condition a secret decides').

value.rs:687-715 fns_widened: composed pairs are widened recursively with widen_at(0, cdepth+1). That resets the data depth, and composed values are never summarized or folded, so compose(g, h) accumulated in a loop, a reduce, or a recursive fold grows without bound. V::leq never holds between successive iterates, because composed-set membership is structural.

builtins.rs:164-176 puts char_at in the 'pure function of content, returns a scalar' group (scalar(deep_all)). The runtime lowers char_at(a, i) to (a).index_get(i) (run.rs emit_builtin_call, 'char_at' arm), which is the general indexer. It returns the list element itself: a closure, a struct or a list.

builtins.rs:169 treats repeat as returning a scalar. The runtime's anubis_repeat (run.rs, 'fn anubis_repeat') returns a List made of the input list's elements repeated when its argument is a list, and a string only otherwise.

eval.rs assign (999-1026) calls set_path(&cur, &segs, v.raise(pc)). Only the stored value is raised by the program counter. set_path inserts a new known map key (eval.rs:1072 for .f and 1116-1118 for [literal]) or adds a struct field (1056-1067) without raising the container's shape label (lab/klab) by pc. The runtime set_at adds the key or field, so the key set and field count depend on the branch.

literal_key (eval.rs:2110-2116) keys maps by the literal's source text. The runtime keys maps by display_string() of the evaluated literal: literal_to_anubis_value makes 1.50 a Float(1.5), which displays as "1.5", and 007 an Int(7), which displays as "7". u64-range literals are reinterpreted as negative i64. MapLiteral (1422-1443), index_read (2134-2146), set_path and the insert/remove paths of mutate all use the raw text.

index_read on structs (eval.rs:2147-2159) treats any literal key whose text does not parse as f64 as a field name. For `true`, it reads field "true", which is missing, and returns PUB Int(0). The runtime index_get (run.rs:1643-1700) reads a field by name only when the index is a Str. A Bool index takes the as_i64() path, so true is position 1, the secret field k.

builtins.rs applies each callback once through cb(it, f, elems, c.lab, p) (63-67, 436-455), so the program counter is only the collection's shape. The runtime's anubis_any, anubis_all, anubis_find, anubis_position, anubis_take_while and anubis_drop_while stop at the first decisive predicate result. Whether the callback runs on element i therefore depends on the predicate results for elements 0..i-1, which here are decided by the secret.

builtins.rs:456-460 runs the sort_by key callback once under pc c.lab. The runtime anubis_sort_by calls the key function twice per comparison inside Rust's sort_by, and the number of comparisons depends on the element order, which here depends on the secret.

A map's key set is labelled lab ⊔ klab (len_label, eval.rs:2077-2085), but nearly every collection builtin in builtins.rs uses only c.lab as both the iteration-count and the result-shape label. That covers map, filter, each, find, any, all, count, flat_map, take_while, drop_while, position, partition, reduce (cb shape and acc.raise), concat, flatten, zip, enumerate, take, drop, chunk and window. The runtime anubis_iter iterates a map's keys, so the number of iterations and the result length equal the number of distinct keys.

builtins.rs:490-494 spreads a list whose items are not individually known as vec![li.all; 6]. Parameters from the seventh on are then padded with PUB: analyze_lambda does args.get(i) or PUB, and a user fn value is resized to its arity with PUB. The runtime anubis_apply passes every element, so p7 = ys[6] = k.

reduce (builtins.rs:548-557) iterates the accumulator fixpoint with `for _ in 0..40` and stops silently when it runs out, joining whatever acc it has. It neither checks convergence nor sets `exhausted`. Every other fixpoint in eval.rs fails closed (LOOP_LIMIT leads to ANUBIS_IFC2_LIMIT).

builtins.rs:147-150 treats keychain_se_last_bind() as a constant PUB scalar. The runtime (keychain_se_runtime.inc.rs) returns a process-global mutex value that cap_acquire_nonexportable writes ("none" before any mint, "soft"/"kc"/"se" after). It is a hidden store written under whatever pc the mint runs at.

The runtime implements password_hash_phc_raw (run.rs emit_builtin_call: "password_hash_phc" | "password_hash_phc_raw"). builtins.rs:173-174 lists a nonexistent "password_hash_raw" and omits password_hash_phc_raw, so builtins::call returns None. eval_call (eval.rs:1644-1648) then looks for a local of that name, finds none, and returns V::bottom(), dropping every argument label.

The runtime anubis_reduce picks the fold function by is_closure() on the two non-list arguments. reduce() (builtins.rs:525-561) analyzes both orders, but runs each callback under pc c.lab only. The label deciding which argument is the closure (x.lab, here SEC) is joined only into the result (`decided`), not into the callbacks' pc.

run.rs:4953-5000 lowers recv.m(args) by pasting the argument expressions into each type arm of a match on the receiver's runtime type, truncated to that method's arity. An argument is therefore evaluated only in arms whose arity reaches it, under the condition 'receiver is of type T'. method_call (eval.rs:1664-1666) evaluates every argument once, before dispatch, under the outer pc.

field_read (eval.rs:2170-2192) reads known[f] (or other) and raises only by b.lab. Unlike index_read (eval.rs:2145, which uses raise(m.klab)), it does not join m.klab, the label deciding whether a computed key equals f. The runtime field_get on a Map looks the key up by name, and a computed key equal to "a" overwrites it in the literal.

MapV treats known[k] as the exact value at key k and `other` as values at keys that are not known. At runtime a computed key whose display string equals a literal key overwrites it: anubis_map_lit keeps the last value, anubis_merge lets the second map win, and after a branch join either side may be present. MapLiteral (eval.rs:1422-1443) never joins `other` into colliding known slots. index_read with a literal key (eval.rs:2136) returns known[k] without `other`. V::join for maps (value.rs:406-423) keeps known[k] from one side only, and merge (builtins.rs:375) is a join. set_path's non-literal-key arm (eval.rs:1120-1128) does join the value into every known slot, so it is the only consistent writer.

IFC v2 treats a panic message as egress only for the panic() builtin (builtins.rs:98-108). The runtime's fail-closed traps also embed operand values in their panic messages: index_get index/length (run.rs:1643-1655), a missing map key, chr code points, factorial n, and the count or width arguments of repeat, substr, pad, take, chunk and times. None of these is modeled.

This is the dual of L14. method_call evaluates every argument before dispatch (eval.rs:1666), but the runtime drops arguments past the chosen arm's arity without evaluating them (run.rs:4966-4977, `want = arity - 1`). q is always a B, whose m takes no argument, so print("x") never runs.

if_value does va.join(vb).raise(clab), and raise_in_place (value.rs:311-313) sets the struct node's lab, which means its type, to SEC even though both alternatives are Acct. method_call then dispatches under pc ⊔ recv.lab (eval.rs:1670). The runtime dispatch depends only on the type name, which is Acct in every case.

Same raise() conflation as O02. The joined list has known items of equal length (2), yet raise(clab) sets the list's lab (its length label) to SEC. iter_count_label = len_label = lab puts the loop body under a secret pc. The runtime iterates exactly two times either way.

builtins.rs:168 puts contains in the scalar(deep_all(args)) group, so the result carries the labels of the map's values. The runtime anubis_contains on a Map (run.rs, 'fn anubis_contains') tests key presence only: `m.iter().any(|(k, _)| k == &n)`.

Stmt::If, While (eval.rs:896 and 1226-1227) and if_value take the condition label as c.deep().control(). The runtime as_bool (run.rs:1557-1569) depends only on a list's or map's length, and is constant true for a struct, enum or closure. The element labels are irrelevant.

compose (builtins.rs:510-515) stores the whole argument values in FnSet.composed. An accumulator acc' = compose(f, acc) therefore nests itself, and each join adds a new pair containing the previous acc. value.rs widening summarizes only lambda capture environments past CLOSURE_DEPTH. Composed pairs are re-widened with depth reset to 0 (fns_widened, value.rs:705-715) and are never folded, so the value's size grows without bound and no fixpoint (the reduce loop, a solve_summary, a for loop) converges.

eval.rs:1422-1443 (Expr::MapLiteral) puts a computed key's value only in MapV.other and leaves known["a"] as it is. index_read (eval.rs:2136) and field_read (eval.rs:2176) return known[k] without joining other. The runtime (run.rs:2885 anubis_map_lit) keys by display_string and keeps the last duplicate, so k=="a" overwrites the literal entry.

value.rs:406-423 (V::join for maps). When a key is known on one side only, the joined known[k] is that side's value (line 413 `None => v.clone()`). It should also join the other side's `other`, because that side's value at key k is described by its `other`. value.rs:539-550 (leq) has the matching gap: it never checks self.other against keys known only in o.
builtins.rs:375 models merge(a,b) as a.join(b). That inherits L02's join gap: m2's computed key overrides m1's known "a" (run.rs:3186 anubis_merge), but the join keeps known["a"]=1.

eval.rs:999-1026 (assign) and set_path eval.rs:1048-1143. A place write raises only the stored value by pc (v.raise(pc), line 1020). Inserting a new map key (lines 1068-1074, 1116-1119) or a new struct field (lines 1056-1067) never raises the container's lab or klab, and V::join unions key and field sets without labelling them. len_label (eval.rs:2077), keys, has_key, for-in, first and the key order all read lab/klab only.

eval.rs:1056-1067 (set_path Seg::Field on a struct) adds the field without raising the struct's lab. The merged value keeps lab=PUB, and len_label (eval.rs:2077) returns lab. At runtime, field_set pushes a new field (run.rs:1741-1744, set_at run.rs:1989-1994), so len(p) is the field count.

eval.rs:2147-2159 (index_read on structs). Any literal key that does not parse as f64 is read as a field name, so `true` reads field "true", which is missing, giving public 0. The runtime index_get (run.rs:1684-1696) uses a name only for Str indexes. Bool(true).as_i64()==1 reads fields[1] by position.

eval.rs:2110-2116 (literal_key) uses the literal's source text ("007", "1.50", "1e0"). The runtime keys maps by display_string of the value: Int(7) gives "7" and Float(1.5) gives "1.5" (run.rs:5580 literal_to_anubis_value, 1788 anubis_float_str). The lexer strips `_` but keeps leading zeros and float spellings (frontend/mod.rs:1428-1500). The read misses known["7"] and gets `other`, which is bottom.

value.rs:758-775 (join_enum) joins payload fields by position and keeps one side's names (lines 769-773). Struct-variant payloads are stored in literal order with parallel field_names (eval.rs:1413-1418; runtime field_get by name, run.rs:1726-1736). Joining {a,b} with {b,a} pairs a with b. value.rs:560-567 (leq) also ignores names.

eval.rs:2170-2192 (field_read). For maps it returns known.get(f) or other and never raises by m.klab. index_read does raise by klab (eval.rs:2145). method_call's fallback (eval.rs:1712-1724) calls the closure read this way under pc = recv.lab only.

builtins.rs:164-176 lists repeat among the content-scalar builtins (scalar(a)). The runtime anubis_repeat (run.rs:2189) returns a list of the original elements when given a list. The scalar result has no fns, so apply (eval.rs:755-804) finds nothing to call.

builtins.rs has no entry for password_hash_phc_raw. It lists "password_hash_raw" (line 174), a name the runtime does not have. The runtime maps "password_hash_phc" | "password_hash_phc_raw" (run.rs:4440). eval_call then falls through builtins::call → None → no local → V::bottom() (eval.rs:1641-1648).

builtins.rs:64-67 (cb) applies every callback under p.pc ⊔ the collection's shape label. any/all/find/position/take_while/drop_while (run.rs:2846-2855, 3058-3094) stop early, and sort_by (run.rs:2859-2875) calls the key function a data-dependent number of times. So whether a later call runs is decided by earlier results (r.deep()), which the analysis never joins into the callback's pc.

value.rs:200-201 (shape_all) gives PUB for a pure scalar, so the fold in widen_at_limit (value.rs:617-626) puts a secret string's content only in tlab. part_of_top (value.rs:179-186) keeps lab=shape, and len_label and type() (eval.rs:2077, builtins.rs:162) read lab. A string's length, and a scalar's kind (int vs string), depend on its content.

value.rs:179-186 (part_of_top) builds a top with an empty FnSet. Widening keeps a folded value's functions in t.fns (value.rs:620-625), but every read of a part drops them: index_read (eval.rs:2163-2165), field_read, elems, bind_pattern and try_value. set_path on a top also never adds a stored closure's fns (eval.rs:1075-1077, 1136-1139). apply (eval.rs:755-804) then calls nothing.

eval.rs:1786-1806 (binary +). When the right operand is a top, `list + top` is modelled as appending one element, with result lab = l.lab. At runtime a top that is a list concatenates (run.rs:1804), so the result length is len(l)+len(r), and r.lab (secret here) is dropped.

builtins.rs:179-203 (min/max). A single argument whose list is None (a top) counts as one candidate, so chooser=PUB and the whole top is returned unchanged. At runtime anubis_seq spreads a single list argument (run.rs:2066-2078), so max picks one element by comparing values, some of them secret.

builtins.rs:486-503 (apply). Only xs.list is spread. A top argument is passed as one argument (lines 497-501), so the callback's second parameter is missing and becomes public 0 (eval.rs:729-733). At runtime anubis_apply spreads any List (run.rs:2876-2881).

builtins.rs:493: for a list with unknown items, `vec![li.all.raise(xs.lab); 6]` spreads only six arguments. A seventh or later parameter is padded with public 0 (eval.rs:729-733 for lambdas, a.resize at eval.rs:778 for user fns). At runtime every element is spread.

eval.rs:2298-2338 (bind_pattern EnumVariant). It takes the payload only from enums whose (type, tag) match the pattern, else public 0. A `let` pattern is irrefutable at runtime (run.rs:3607-3618 ignores the test), and payload_expr (run.rs:5520-5524) reads position i of any enum value.
eval.rs:1378-1397 inserts struct literal fields into a BTreeMap, so the last duplicate wins. The runtime keeps both (run.rs:5236-5277), and field_get finds the first (run.rs:1726-1729).

IFC v2 treats panic(msg) as egress (builtins.rs:98-108), but not the runtime's own fail-closed traps. Their messages embed operand values: index_get's missing key (run.rs:1674), out-of-range index and length, chr code point, repeat/take/substr counts.

eval.rs:1145-1196 (exec_loop). loop_cache is keyed by (loop statement, frame depth), not by call context. A later call whose entry state is ⊑ an earlier call's entry reuses that call's exit state and return value (lines 1148-1166). A larger entry is joined with the previous one (lines 1169-1175). So the public call total([2,3]) gets the secret call's result.

eval.rs:508-549 with CONTEXTS_PER_CALLEE=12 (eval.rs:31). From the 13th distinct argument context on, every call shares one summary whose arguments are the join. A public call then receives a result computed from another call's secret argument. Any change of known list length or map key set makes a new context.

eval.rs:894-896 (Stmt::If), 1225-1228 (while), 1742-1744 (&&, ||), 1821-1823 (if_value) and 1352-1355 (Unary) use c.deep() for the condition. Runtime truthiness (run.rs:1557-1569) is list, map or string non-emptiness (shape), and always true for enum, struct and closure.

eval.rs:1268-1279 (exec_loop_solve) adds cnt_at into lift_loop for every later iteration, and the for variable is bound raised by that pc (eval.rs:1257). A `continue` skips only the rest of its own iteration, and later iterations run regardless. Only `break` decides whether later iterations run.

eval.rs:1832 (if_value `.raise(clab)`) and value.rs:311-343 (raise_in_place) raise every shape label, including struct type, tag and list length, even when all branches have the same shape. method_call then uses pc = recv.lab (eval.rs:1670), and for-in uses len_label (eval.rs:2106).

The loop widens v to a nested value about DATA_DEPTH (32) deep regardless of the iteration count. The recursive walker then creates a distinct call context per nesting level, each solved to a fixpoint (eval.rs:481-610). Cost grows about 2x per level. No ANUBIS_IFC2_LIMIT is raised, because STEP_BUDGET ticks count statements, not value operations.

The second loop's fixpoint (eval.rs:1198-1303) joins g with g[0] each round over a value up to 32 levels deep. The joins and leq over the nested value blow up before LOOP_LIMIT or STEP_BUDGET trigger ANUBIS_IFC2_LIMIT.

eval.rs exec_loop_solve (about lines 1274-1279): after each iteration it sets next.cond = entry.cond and joins only the break/continue pcs into lift_loop. The header's own decision clab is never joined in. At runtime, iteration k+1's header runs only when iteration k's header was true, so it runs under clab. In the analysis it runs at the entry pc, so side effects in the header (expression-position push/pop/insert/remove) and egress in the header are unlabeled in later rounds. Fix: treat the condition-false exit as a break at clab, i.e. next.lift_loop |= clab (and the pattern decision d for while-let).

Same as CTL-L1. Under D1 the while header is an egress site that runs under the previous iteration's secret condition, but exec_loop_solve evaluates the header from a head state whose cond was reset to entry.cond. So tick is called at pc PUB with key (tick,[SEC],PUB) and its println is not flagged.
Same as CTL-L1, in the LoopKind::WhileLet arm. The scrutinee of round k+1 runs only if round k's pattern decision d (SEC here) matched, but it is evaluated from head with cond = entry.cond.

eval.rs Interp::apply, the fns.composed loop (about lines 796-799). Each composed pair is applied with self.apply(&h, args, p) and self.apply(&g, [inner], p), using the caller's path p. It is not raised by f.lab.control(), unlike the builtins arm (sub path with cond ⊔ f.lab) and the user/closure arms (pc ⊔ f.lab). V::raise_in_place does not touch fns.composed either, so the components keep lab PUB. The if-value raises c.lab to SEC, but which pair runs is never charged to the pc.

eval.rs method_call (about lines 1665-1666) evaluates every argument with the caller's path before dispatch, at pc p.pc(). The runtime (run.rs 4957-5000) inlines each lowered argument into each type's match arm and passes only arity-1 of them, and the fallback passes all of them. So which arguments run depends on the receiver's runtime type (recv.lab), and an argument beyond the chosen method's arity never runs.

builtins.rs: any/all/count/position (about lines 451-455), find/min_by/max_by (446-450) and filter/take_while/drop_while (436-440) apply the callback once via cb(it,&f,[elems],c.lab,p), so the callback's pc is only the collection's shape label. At runtime anubis_any uses Iterator::any (run.rs 2850), and all, find, position and take_while also stop at the first decisive result. Whether the callback runs on element i+1 therefore depends on its result for element i (r.deep(), SEC here).
Same as CTL-L6 (the any/all/count/position arm of builtins.rs applies the callback once under c.lab).

builtins.rs sort_by (about lines 456-460) applies the key callback once under pc c.lab. At runtime (anubis_sort_by) the comparator calls the key function a number of times that depends on the element order. Here that order depends on s, and the key results are SEC.

eval.rs set_path (about lines 1048-1143), reached from assign(). A place assignment that inserts a NEW map key (Seg::Index with a literal key, or Seg::Field on a map) raises the stored value by pc. It never raises the container's shape label (out.lab, the key set) or klab by pc. The root is then stored by st.assign without raising the shape. At the merge the map joins to {a, b} with lab PUB, so len/has_key/keys and for-loop counts are PUB. builtins::mutate insert/remove do raise out.lab/klab by pc; set_path does not. The same happens for a missing struct field added by p.f = v (see CTL-L10).

Same as CTL-L9, in the Seg::Field arm for structs. The runtime adds a missing field (RUN set_at), and len_val of a Struct is its field count (run.rs 1766). The analysis's len_label returns the struct's lab, which set_path never raises by pc.

builtins.rs mutate: pop (about lines 604-628) and remove (659-683) raise out.lab by pc only when cur.list or cur.map is Some. When cur is `top` they leave its shape label unchanged. Here big has more than MAX_NODES=256 nodes, so widen at the call folds each inner list into top, and b[0] is top. push and insert do raise a top's lab by pc; pop and remove do not.

builtins.rs exit (about lines 109-122) sets p.st = None without recording an exit pc the way do_return records ret_at. merge() therefore does not lift the continuation, and the println after the if is analyzed at pc PUB. The same program with `return;` in place of exit(0) is refused by NEW with ANUBIS_IMPLICIT_FLOW.

builtins.rs sort (about lines 266-269) returns list_of(elems(c), c.lab). Which element lands at each position depends on comparing every element's content (anubis_value_cmp, lexicographic over lists), but the result is labeled only with the collection's shape. For scalar elements the join happens to cover it. For compound elements the inner per-position labels stay PUB (here the second component is 1 ⊔ 2, PUB). Fix: raise the list shape by elems(c).deep(), as unique and sort_by do.

eval.rs exec_loop_solve takes only hp.exits.ret_at from the header path. hp.exits.brk, brk_at, cnt and cnt_at are silently dropped. The runtime lowers while-let as `loop { let t = e; if test { .. } else { break } }` (run.rs 3713-3729), so a break or continue inside the scrutinee exits the user's loop carrying its state. Here the break state holds log with the secret-conditioned push, and it is lost from the loop exit. The control without the break (the same push under the same condition, yielding None) is refused by NEW.

eval.rs len_label (about lines 2077-2085) returns v.lab. For a `top` value v.lab is only the shape label: the fold builds V::top(shape_all()) with tlab = deep(), and shape_all of a pure scalar is PUB. A string's length is its content (tlab SEC). is_empty and iter_count_label (the for-loop count) use the same function. The control with a small (unfolded) list is refused by NEW.

eval.rs exec_loop (about lines 1145-1196). loop_cache is keyed by (statement address, frame depth) and reused whenever entry.leq(&cached.entry). The cached exit state, frame ret and ret_at computed for g(s) are handed to the analysis of g(5), whose entry (x PUB) is ⊑ the cached one (x SEC). When the entry is not ⊑, the 're-entered with a larger state' path still joins the previous entry from the other call context. The result is order-dependent: with the two calls swapped NEW accepts, and without the loop (the same g with an if) NEW accepts.

Same loop_cache as CTL-O1, carrying the condition label this time. cnt is first analyzed under pc SEC (inside the secret if-value). The later cnt(3) at pc PUB hits the cached loop, whose exit state has cond = SEC. So `let r = 5` after the loop is raised SEC and the public call's result becomes secret.

eval.rs exec_loop_solve (about lines 1268-1279) joins cnt_at into next.lift_loop, the same as brk_at. A continue under a secret condition therefore lifts every later iteration, including the loop variable binding and an egress at the top of the body. After a continue, the next iteration starts exactly as it does after the body's end. A for-loop's count is fixed, and a while re-evaluates its condition either way. The only values that differ are those assigned after the continue point, and the in-body lift already raises them. break must lift; continue need not.

eval.rs match_value (about lines 1866-1875) joins the pattern_decision of ALL sub-arms into d before trying any arm, and every arm runs under outer.cond ⊔ d. Arm 0 runs exactly when its own pattern matches, which depends only on k (public). The later arm's `[_, 5]` test on s makes arm 0 look secret-controlled. The comment says 'decided by every pattern and guard before it', but the code joins the later ones too. Fix: accumulate d arm by arm, joining arm i's pattern decision after arm i.

eval.rs call (about lines 508-549). After CONTEXTS_PER_CALLEE = 12 distinct argument contexts, every later call of the callee shares one summary context whose arguments are the join of all later calls' arguments. One call with a secret argument therefore makes the result of every later public call secret. The same happens with a loop in the callee.

Not traced. It needs a scalar joined with a nested list that grows by one level each iteration (m = [m, j] starting from 0), under two nested loops. The single-loop form takes 16 ms, and the same nest starting from [] takes 10 ms. The inner loop is probably re-solved on every outer round, each time growing toward DATA_DEPTH = 32 with O(size) or worse join/leq/widen work, but this was not confirmed.

Likely (hypothesis, not traced) that FnSet.composed nesting is never folded. value.rs fns_widened widens composed components with widen_at(0, ..), restarting the data depth at 0 and ignoring the reduced MAX_NODES limit. So compose(inc, c) in a loop grows the loop-head value every round and never becomes ⊑ the previous head.

eval.rs:1145-1166 (exec_loop): loop_cache is keyed by (loop statement address, frame depth) and does not include the call context. A later call to the same function at the same frame depth whose loop-entry state is below an earlier context's entry (entry.leq(&r.entry)) reuses that earlier context's exit and frame return. Here the public list (after filter/map it has items None) is below the secret one, so `summarize(public)` gets the secret loop result.

eval.rs:1167-1175 (exec_loop): when a loop is re-entered with a state that is not below the cached one, it is solved from `prev.entry.join(&entry).widen()`, where prev is the last result cached for this (loop, frame depth) from ANY caller context. The previous context's secret `xs` is joined into this call's `xs`, so `xs[i]` and `best` come out secret for the public call.

eval.rs:1268-1279 (exec_loop_solve): `lift = brk_at ⊔ cnt_at` is joined into `next.lift_loop` for every later iteration. That is right for `break`, which ends the iterations, but wrong for `continue`: a continue skips only the rest of the current body, and the next iteration runs regardless. Data written after the continue point already carries the label through `merge`.

eval.rs:1891-1902 (match_value): a guard's label is joined into `d`, and `d` is the pc of EVERY later sub-arm. That ignores whether a later arm's pattern can match a value that reached the guarded arm. `Ev::Tick` and `Ev::Quit` are disjoint from `Ev::Try(g)`, so a failed guard can never fall through to them.

eval.rs:2226-2247 (pattern_decision, Pattern::EnumVariant): the loop `for e in v.enums.values()` checks the pattern's sub-patterns against the payload of EVERY variant the value may hold, not only the pattern's own (enum_name, variant). The literal `0` in `Cmd::Move(0)` is therefore tested against `Cmd::Auth(pin)`'s secret payload. Because match_value then joins every sub-arm's decision into `d` (eval.rs:1871-1875), all arms run under a secret pc.

eval.rs:1670 (method_call): `pc = p.pc() ⊔ recv.lab`, and the result is raised by recv.lab. recv.lab is the node label, and it is secret whenever the value was qualified `secret<..>`, selected under a secret branch, or returned after a secret-conditioned return. Dispatch, however, depends only on the runtime type name. When the receiver can be only one struct type (or only one enum type, whatever its tag), the method that runs is fixed.

eval.rs:2061-2070 (qualify): a type containing `secret<` anywhere (the ty::is_secret substring test) raises the WHOLE value, including the Option/Result tag and a list's length. For `Result<secret<str>, str>` only the Ok payload is secret, and whether Ok or Err comes back is decided by the public `path == ""`. try_value (eval.rs:1947-1956) then takes d = v.lab = SEC, and the rest of `start` runs under lift_ret = SEC.

eval.rs:895-896 (Stmt::If), eval.rs:1822-1823 (if_value), eval.rs:1226-1227 (While) and eval.rs:1744 (&&, ||) all use `c.deep()` as the control label. The runtime's as_bool on a List or Map depends only on emptiness, which is the node's `lab` (len_label). On a struct, enum or closure it is constant true. deep() also takes in every element's content label.

eval.rs:2196-2198 (pattern_decision): `if v.top { return v.deep() }`. For a value that has been folded into `top` (DATA_DEPTH, MAX_NODES or SUMMARY_DEPTH widening), matching an enum-variant, struct, wildcard or binding pattern depends only on the shape label `lab`, but the code returns the content label (tlab) as well. The recursive structure built in the loop is folded, so every `match` in the walk becomes secret-decided.

eval.rs:508-549 (call) with CONTEXTS_PER_CALLEE = 12: from the 13th distinct argument context on, a callee has one summary context per pc, whose arguments are the join of every later call's arguments. The secret payroll list (13th context) and the public refunds list (14th) share it, so `avg(refunds)` returns secret.

value.rs:687-704 and eval.rs:422-438: a closure nested deeper than CLOSURE_DEPTH (3) in captures is replaced by Clo::Summary, and there is ONE summary env per lambda id (Interp::summaries). Every snapshot of `|x| g(f(x))` inside `then` is joined into it. The innermost stage of `plain` is summarized, so it may apply `|x| x + salt` from the other pipeline.

value.rs:457-466 and 604-626 (widen_from with MAX_NODES = 256): at the call boundary the 52-record list (313 nodes) is re-widened at halving depth limits until it fits, so every record is folded into `top` with tlab = its deep label. field_read then returns part_of_top (content SEC) for `u.name`, and the per-field labels are lost.

eval.rs:1113-1131 (set_path, Seg::Index on a map; the Seg::Field-on-map arm at 1068-1074 is the same): a place assignment that inserts a new key raises the inserted VALUE by the pc (assign passes v.raise(pc)), but raises neither the map's `lab` nor its `klab`. After the branches merge, V::join unions the known key sets. len_label (lab ⊔ klab), has_key, keys, entries and `for k in m` then all see a public key set, although whether `b` exists was decided by the secret. mutate("insert") raises out.lab by pc (builtins.rs:651), and set_path should do the same.

eval.rs:1054-1067 (set_path, Seg::Field on a struct): writing a missing field adds it at runtime (run.rs field set adds the field), and len_val on a Struct is the field count. IFC v2 inserts the field with a pc-raised value but does not raise the struct's `lab`. join_fields unions the field sets, so len/is_empty (len_label = lab) are public.

eval.rs:2110-2116 (literal_key) uses the literal's source text ("01") as the map key. The runtime keys maps by display_string() of the key value, and Int(1) displays as "1". IFC v2 therefore reads known["01"] (public 5) while the runtime reads key "1", which holds the secret. The same mismatch exists for any literal whose text is not its display form (for example 1.50 or u64-range literals).

value.rs:106-120: ListV keeps `items` and also `all`, the join of the items, which shares the children. The derived Hash/PartialEq/Ord on V/ListV, used for CallKey in memo/in_progress/contexts (eval.rs:497-507), visit both, so the cost doubles per nesting level. all_fns (value.rs:469-500), raise_in_place and release_in_place also traverse both. The same nesting with no call is fast (21 ms), which is consistent with the hashing of the call key. This is inferred from code and timing, not profiled.
value.rs:311-343 (raise_in_place): under a secret pc, `let w = v` raises v. Rc::make_mut on the shared ListV clones and recurses into both `all` and `items`, allocating about 2^depth nodes.

The recursive `insert` result does not settle: ANUBIS_IFC2_LIMIT 'a recursive call did not settle' (eval.rs:603-605 or 641-643, LOOP_LIMIT 60). Trace evidence from ANUBIS_IFC2_TRACE_V on scratch/s1.anb: the length of the printed result value grows 1151, 2921, 6461, 13541, 27701, 56021 and then collapses to 12677 and 2909 before growing again. The MAX_NODES re-fold at halving depth limits (value.rs:457-466) is not a monotone widening: a bigger value is folded shallower, and leq() returns false for a folded `top` against a structured node (value.rs:512-514), so `r.leq(&before)` never holds. The secret payload drives the growth (tags become secret through pattern_decision(top) = deep, OR-09). The same program with i64 payloads settles (p007.anb).
